claims.text: Summary: This paper addresses the critical challenge of uncertainty quantification in neural radiance fields for safety-critical applications.

The authors introduce Evidential Neural Radiance Fields, a probabilistic approach that quantifies both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties from a single forward pass without compromising rendering quality or incurring significant computational overhead.
The method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on three standardized benchmarks for both scene reconstruction fidelity and uncertainty estimation quality.
First method to separately capture both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties in NeRF
Single forward pass uncertainty estimation
State-of-the-art performance on standardized benchmarks
Hung, H.-H., Do, H.-P., Li, Y.-H., & Huang, C.-C.
TimeNeRF: Building Generalizable Neural Radiance Fields across Time from Few-Shot Input Views.
Summary: TimeNeRF presents a generalizable neural rendering approach for rendering novel views at arbitrary viewpoints and times from few input views.
The method combines multi-view stereo, neural radiance fields, and disentanglement strategies to enable temporal 3D scene modeling without per-scene optimization.
The approach excels at creating realistic novel views that transition smoothly across different times, capturing intricate natural scene changes from dawn to dusk.
Few-shot generalizable NeRF for temporal scene modeling
Smooth transitions across different times of day
Huang, A., Sonawane, P., Thorat, Y., & Rao, Y.
Summary: This comparative study examines three accelerated NeRF variants (DS-NeRF, TensoRF, and HashNeRF) in low-compute, low-data regimes.
The authors explore extensions including depth-supervision loss for TensoRF, feature-decoding MLP ablation, and four architectural variants of HashNeRF color and density networks.
While none of the extensions conclusively outperform published baselines under iso-time evaluation, the experiments characterize which extensions transfer to constrained settings.
Systematic comparison of accelerated NeRF variants
Depth-supervision extensions for reduced view counts
Architectural variants for low-cost deployment
R., Siddartha, R., Venkata Girish, R.
GN-FR: Generalizable Neural Radiance Fields for Flare Removal.
Summary: This work addresses flare removal as a multi-view image problem using generalizable neural radiance fields.
The proposed GN-FR framework incorporates Flare-occupancy Mask Generation, View Sampler, and Point Sampler modules within the Generalizable NeRF Transformer framework.
The method introduces a masking loss function for unsupervised learning and presents a new 3D multi-view flare dataset with 17 real flare scenes and 782 images.
First NeRF-based approach to flare removal
Unsupervised learning with masking loss
New 3D multi-view flare dataset
Xiao, W., Chierchia, R., Santa Cruz, R., Li, X., Ahmedt-Aristizabal, D., Salvado, O., Fookes, C., & Lebrat, L.
Neural Radiance Fields for the Real World: A Survey.
Summary: This comprehensive survey compiles key theoretical advancements and alternative scene representations in NeRF research.
It investigates emerging challenges, explores applications in reconstruction, highlights NeRF's impact on computer vision and robotics, and reviews essential datasets and toolkits.
The survey identifies gaps in the literature and discusses open challenges with directions for future research.
Comprehensive review of NeRF theoretical advancements
Analysis of real-world applications and challenges
Identification of research gaps and future directions
Wagner, V., Bullinger, S., Bodensteiner, C., & Arens, M.
Semantic Neural Radiance Fields for Multi-Date Satellite Data.

Summary: This work proposes a satellite-specific NeRF model capable of obtaining a three-dimensional semantic representation from multi-date satellite images with corresponding pixel-wise semantic labels.

The model demonstrates robustness in improving noisy input labels and enhances color prediction by utilizing semantic information to address temporal inconsistencies caused by non-stationary categories such as vehicles.
First semantic NeRF for satellite data
Improved handling of temporal inconsistencies
New labeled dataset for multi-view satellite images
Qazi, A., Basit, A., & Iqbal, A.
NeuGen: Amplifying the 'Neural' in Neural Radiance Fields for Domain Generalization.
Summary: This paper proposes integrating a brain-inspired normalization technique called Neural Generalization (NeuGen) into leading NeRF architectures including MVSNeRF and GeoNeRF.
NeuGen extracts domain-invariant features, enhancing models' generalization capabilities across diverse scenes and conditions.
The approach demonstrates improved performance on benchmarks across diverse datasets and state-of-the-art NeRF architectures.
Brain-inspired normalization technique for NeRF
Improved rendering quality across varied scenes
Gao, C., Wang, Y., Kim, C., Huang, J.-B., & Kopf, J.
Planar Reflection-Aware Neural Radiance Fields.
Summary: This work addresses NeRF's limitation in handling complex planar reflections by introducing a reflection-aware NeRF that jointly models planar reflectors and explicitly casts reflected rays.
The method proposes sparse edge regularization to utilize true sources of reflections, obtaining accurate scene geometry.
The approach enables both clean, reflection-free views and highly detailed reflection reconstruction.
Joint modeling of planar reflectors and scene geometry
Sparse edge regularization for accurate reflections
Dual capability: reflection-free and detailed reflection views
Gu, S., Qiu, Y.-K., Tang, Y.-M., Wu, A., & Zheng, W.-S.
MaintaAvatar: A Maintainable Avatar Based on Neural Radiance Fields by Continual Learning.
Summary: This work addresses the practical challenge of updating human avatars while maintaining the ability to render past appearances.
The proposed MaintaAvatar resolves catastrophic forgetting issues through a Global-Local Joint Storage Module and a Pose Distillation Module.
The model requires only limited data collection for quick fine-tuning while avoiding color bleeding and incorrect pose issues.
Continual learning framework for maintainable avatars
Pose Distillation Module for avoiding catastrophic forgetting
Barreiro, A., Marí, R., Redondo, R., Haro, G., & Bosch, C.
ShinyNeRF: Digitizing Anisotropic Appearance in Neural Radiance Fields.
Summary: This paper introduces ShinyNeRF, a novel framework capable of handling both isotropic and anisotropic reflections for 3D digitization of cultural heritage.
The method jointly estimates surface normals, tangents, specular concentration, and anisotropy magnitudes of an Anisotropic Spherical Gaussian distribution.
Experimental results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in digitizing anisotropic specular reflections with plausible physical interpretations.
First NeRF framework for anisotropic reflections
Joint estimation of multiple material properties
State-of-the-art performance on specular surface digitization
